purpose: Define how question applicability, evidence, contextual evidence and gender-neutral wording should be represented in questions.json.
principles: Gender-neutral questions must have gender-neutral default evidence text.
Gender-specific evidence must only be shown when its applicability condition is satisfied.
Question applicability, evidence applicability and recommendation applicability are separate concepts.
A question being relevant to everyone does not mean every supporting evidence source applies identically to every person.
Do not silently convert biological-sex-specific evidence into generic claims.
Evidence records should preserve source, review date and evidence scope.
Historical rationale and modern evidence must remain distinguishable.

question_applicability.all: Question is applicable to the general questionnaire population.
question_applicability.female_context: Question is applicable only where the person's selected context makes female reproductive/menopause information relevant.
question_applicability.male_context: Question is applicable only where male-specific context is relevant.
question_applicability.conditional: Applicability depends on another profile answer or questionnaire response.

applicability_model.evidence_applicability: Each evidence source may specify whether it is universal or context-specific.
applicability_model.recommendation_applicability: Recommendation rules are maintained separately from question applicability and evidence applicability.

default.summary: Short, user-facing, gender-neutral explanation where the question is universal.

validation_rules.rule: If question applicability is all, evidence.default.summary must not contain gender-specific terms unless the statement is explicitly universal.
Gender-specific evidence must be stored under contextual evidence with an explicit condition.
Every source must have a title, URL, evidence scope and review date before publication.
Historical rationale must not be presented as modern scientific evidence.
A source supporting why a question is relevant does not automatically support a numerical scoring relationship.
Q46 and Q47 remain conditionally applicable and must not be presented to respondents for whom the menopause context is not applicable.

example.text: How would you describe your sleep?

default.summary: Sleep quality can influence daytime energy, cognitive function and emotional wellbeing.

contextual.summary: Sleep can also change during the menopausal transition as hormonal changes occur.

implementation_note: The example intentionally contains no invented source URLs. Evidence sources should be populated during the question-by-question scientific review.
